facts.eden: Eden was the garden where God placed the first man and woman.
facts.gaza: Gaza was a major Philistine city on the Mediterranean coast.
facts.cana: Cana is the town where Jesus turned water into wine.
facts.moab: Moab was a kingdom east of the Dead Sea, home to Ruth.
facts.tyre: Tyre was a wealthy Phoenician port city on the coast.
facts.gath: Gath was a Philistine city and the hometown of Goliath.
facts.nile: The Nile is the great river of Egypt central to the Exodus story.
facts.zion: Zion is a hill in Jerusalem often used as a name for the city itself.
facts.edom: Edom was a kingdom south of the Dead Sea, descended from Esau.
facts.egypt: Egypt is the land where Israel was enslaved before the Exodus.
facts.sinai: Sinai is the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments.
facts.judea: Judea was the region around Jerusalem in Jesus' time.
facts.babel: Babel was the site where a tower was built and languages confused.
facts.sodom: Sodom was a city destroyed for its wickedness in Genesis.
facts.endor: Endor was a village where Saul consulted a medium.
facts.haran: Haran was the city Abraham's family settled in before Canaan.
facts.joppa: Joppa was a port city where Jonah set sail to flee God.
facts.sheba: Sheba was a kingdom whose queen visited Solomon.
facts.horeb: Horeb is another name for the mountain where Moses met God.
facts.berea: Berea was a city whose people were noted for studying scripture.
facts.canaan: Canaan was the land promised by God to Abraham's descendants.
facts.hebron: Hebron is where Abraham and Sarah were buried.
facts.bethel: Bethel is where Jacob dreamed of a stairway reaching to heaven.
facts.gilead: Gilead was a hilly region east of the Jordan River.
facts.goshen: Goshen was the fertile region in Egypt where Israel settled.
facts.ararat: Ararat is the mountain where Noah's ark came to rest.
facts.shiloh: Shiloh was the site where the tabernacle stood for many years.
facts.gilgal: Gilgal was Israel's first camp after crossing into Canaan.
facts.carmel: Carmel is the mountain where Elijah defeated the prophets of Baal.
facts.emmaus: Emmaus is the village where Jesus appeared after his resurrection.
facts.midian: Midian was a region where Moses lived before returning to Egypt.
facts.patmos: Patmos is the island where John received the book of Revelation.
facts.tarsus: Tarsus was the birthplace of the apostle Paul.
facts.gibeon: Gibeon was a city whose people tricked Joshua into a treaty.
facts.jericho: Jericho is the city whose walls fell after Israel marched around it.
facts.galilee: Galilee is the region where Jesus spent much of his ministry.
facts.nineveh: Nineveh was the capital of Assyria where Jonah preached.
facts.bethany: Bethany is the village near Jerusalem where Lazarus lived.
facts.samaria: Samaria was a region between Judea and Galilee.
facts.antioch: Antioch was a city where believers were first called Christians.
facts.corinth: Corinth was a Greek city where Paul founded a church.
facts.ephesus: Ephesus was a major city in Asia Minor with an early church.
facts.calvary: Calvary is the hill outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified.
facts.babylon: Babylon was the empire that conquered Judah and exiled its people.
facts.galatia: Galatia was a region in Asia Minor that received a letter from Paul.
